discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the creation of moiré flat-band quantum materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: MacDonald (with Bistritzer) predicted in 2011 that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, bilayer graphene develops nearly flat electronic bands in which interactions dominate. Andrei's scanning-probe work on twisted graphene showed that the twist angle controls van Hove singularities and electron localisation. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built magic-angle devices and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a lone carbon sheet, tunable with a gate voltage. That result launched 'twistronics'. Moiré van der Waals heterostructures now host correlated insulators, orbital ferromagnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators without magnetic field. One device can be tuned across a whole phase diagram. This changed how condensed-matter physicists everywhere study strongly correlated electrons: clean, gate-tunable 2D platforms that are measured with transport, noise and optics.
